title: FLICK: an optimized plate reader-based assay to infer cell death kinetics
protocol: Plate cells into 96 well, optical bottom, black-walled plates according to experimental design.
Include an additional T0 control plate.
Ensure accurate counting and seeding of cells for consistent data between replicates.
Perform two technical replicates on the same plate to account for plating bias.
Consider biological replicates on separate plates or experiments performed on subsequent days.
Culture cell line of interest according to established protocols.
Dilute cells to the appropriate concentration in cell culture media that allows for proper seeding density.
Resuspend cells by gently pipetting up and down.
Add 90 μl of cell suspension to plates.
Place plates in incubator at 37°C and 5% CO2 to adhere overnight (4–18 h).
Prepare a 1% Triton-X permeabilization buffer in sterile PBS.
Prepare a 10× SYTOX solution by diluting 5 mM SYTOX in culture media as needed for the experimental design.
Dilute compounds of interest to 10× their final desired concentration in the 10× SYTOX solution.
Create vehicle control at 10× its final concentration in 10× SYTOX solution.
For dose-response experiments, create serial dilutions of drugs in round-bottom plates at 10× concentrations.
Add 10 μL of SYTOX+compound (or vehicle) solution to experimental wells.
Add 10 μL of 10× SYTOX only solution to T0 control plate wells.
Ensure the final well volume is 100 μL with 1× SYTOX and 1× compound (or vehicle).
Add 10 μL of 1% Triton-X permeabilization buffer to all T0 plate wells.
Incubate the T0 plate at 37°C in a 5% CO2 incubator for >2 h or as optimized.
Quantify the raw fluorescence of dead cells at chosen time points.
Lys cells using Triton-X buffer to quantify total cell fluorescence at the end of the assay.
Set the fluorescence plate reader to appropriate excitation, emission, and gain settings for the chosen SYTOX concentration.
Take an initial reading for experimental plates.
Store the plate in the incubator at 37°C and 5% CO2 until the next time point.
Measure fluorescence once the T0 control plate is fully permeabilized (step 10).
Discard the plate after measuring total starting fluorescence.
Continue taking measurements at selected time points until the end of the experiment.
Maintain time points approximately 4 hours apart, ensuring consistency across biological replicates.
Prepare fresh 1% Triton-X permeabilization buffer prior to reading the final time point.
Add 10 μL of 1% permeabilization buffer to each well after the final measurement.
Incubate the plate for more than 2 hours at 37°C and 5% CO2 for cell lysis.
Take a final fluorescence measurement once all wells are fully lysed.
Check the plate for complete lysis under a microscope before taking the total cell count measurement.
